# Child Activation Functions

A reusable compute definition for preparing child documents with independently declared parties and explicit identity mappings. It also retains legacy construction using the parent’s role names and inherits activation, party-access, admission and amendment helpers. Functions run when called; this type alone does not establish an automatic trigger or caller permission.

The parent or configurer is the document in whose context a function executes, including a nested instruction’s own document. Paths within `child` refer to the child being prepared.

## Explicit child preparation

`prepareChild(child, mapping, suppliedRoles)` returns a modified child. `child` and `mapping` default to `{}`; `suppliedRoles` defaults to `[]`. `bindChild(child, mapping)` delegates to it with no supplied roles.

The child must have no `/contracts/initialized` value and must declare the exact Activation Clause type at `/clauses/activation/type`. Otherwise preparation rejects with `CHILD_ALREADY_INITIALIZED` or `CHILD_ACTIVATION_REQUIRED`.

Party declarations come from the child’s `/clauses/activation/parameters/parties`; configurer identities come from the executing document’s `/activation/parties`.

- `mapping` keys are child role names. Each value is either a configurer role name selecting its party, or an explicit Party value. There is no automatic same-name mapping.
- Every declared child role needs a mapping unless listed in `suppliedRoles`. A supplied role must be declared and must not also be mapped; its declaration is retained for separate supply.
- Configurer parties, declarations and mappings must be objects, and both rosters must be nonempty. Unknown roles and missing mappings reject. Child role names must be nonempty text without `.`, `/`, `~` or `__`.
- Mapped parties require `lead/channel` and a nonempty, duplicate-free `readerKeys` list containing nonempty text. They must be Party values compatible with the child declaration through specialization.
- Every configurer party’s main identity must remain represented in the resulting child roster. Main identity means identical `lead/channel` identity and the same primary `readerKeys` set, regardless of order. Display names and business descriptions do not establish this identity. Child role names may differ from configurer role names.

Preparation replaces the child’s declared parties with the resolved roster. It preserves existing child `accessPaths`, defaulting that list to `[]`, and appends references to each access document named by the parent’s `/activation/accessPaths`, also defaulting to `[]`. References are placed at `/timelineAccess/configurerN`, where numbering starts at the current child access-path count. An occupied target rejects with `CHILD_ACCESS_PATH_CONFLICT`.

For resolved parties having `lead/channel`, preparation writes lead transports to `/contracts/<role>` and additional representative transports to `/contracts/<role>__<repId>`. An existing identical transport is allowed; a different existing value rejects with `CHILD_CHANNEL_CONFLICT`. Parties without a lead channel remain in the roster but are excluded from this transport-installation pass. Other child activation parameters, including `readers`, `required` and `frozen`, are retained.

## Legacy construction

`activateChild(child, frozen, readerNames, roles)` uses parent role names directly. `roles` and `readerNames` default to `[]`; `frozen` is Boolean with no declared default.

If the executing document has no `/activation`, it returns `child` unchanged. Otherwise, empty `roles` selects every parent party; a nonempty list selects only those roles. Only readers explicitly named in `readerNames` are copied. Missing parent roles or readers reject with `CHILD_PARTY_NOT_IN_PARENT` or `CHILD_READER_NOT_IN_PARENT`.

The function constructs child `/timelineAccess/grant0`, `grant1`, and subsequent references from the parent’s access paths and replaces the child’s `timelineAccess` value. It replaces `/clauses/activation` with an Activation Clause, preserving existing parameters except that `parties`, `readers`, `accessPaths` and `frozen` are set from this call. Existing `required` is retained, defaulting to `[]`. It writes all selected lead and representative transports into `/contracts`, overwriting matching keys. Unlike `prepareChild`, this legacy path does not reject an initialized child or check access-target and channel conflicts.

## Inherited activation and access behavior

The inherited runtime uses `/activation` for authoritative activation state. `computeState` derives `accessReady` and `functional` from access checks, `termsAccepted` from required approvals and unchanged agreed fields, and `active` from both conditions plus the document not being `closed`. Its statuses are `WAITING_FOR_ACCESS`, `SUSPENDED_ACCESS`, `AWAITING_ACCEPTANCE`, `ACTIVE` and `CLOSED`; `everActivated` distinguishes initial access waiting from later suspension. Missing approval entries are treated as unapproved by these checks, and absent `required` defaults to an empty list.

`accessValid` checks lead and representative transports. External Channel transports bypass its timeline-access matching. Other transports must be Timeline Channels: each needs a matching Timeline Access document with the same timeline and provider and at least one allowed key from every reader group. Groups comprise named `readers`, party `readerKeys` and representative `readerKeys`; each group’s keys are alternatives. Merely copying access references does not change provider-owned permissions.

`approve` and `approveWithTerms` require `call/requireExactDocumentVersion` to be true, a party-lead `call/channel`, the current `revision`, valid participant access and, when negotiation paths exist, the current `termsRef`. Repeated approval returns successfully without another acceptance event. New approval records acceptance and emits Terms Accepted; it does not necessarily activate the document. `commitState` handles activation and access-transition events, while `refresh` initializes terms when absent, commits derived state and refreshes admission-access readiness.

`requireActive` checks active state and current access when `/activation` exists; with `workflow` true it also checks the invoking channel against current party and representative names. `businessReady` checks required approvals, agreed fields, access and closure. Both helpers explicitly allow their no-activation case; that exception is not evidence that an arbitrary absent state means active.

`updateParty` requires exact review, an unfrozen roster and a party-lead caller. The optional `party` defaults to that caller. Existing parties can only update themselves; adding a party requires `allowNewParties`. A valid replacement lead channel, representative names, participant access and nonconflicting contracts are required. Success clears approvals, advances `revision`, and makes a new party required. `frozen` also blocks `admitApprovedParties`, which additionally checks `expectedRevision`, configured admission approvers, identity preservation and access. Admission access requests can affect readiness before admission completes; Party Access Update Requested is a request, not permission evidence or completed admission.

Inherited access installation validates 1–16 Timeline Access documents, their provider channel, initialization/history markers and executable policy, deduplicates by original document identity, and registers refresh channels. Inherited amendment helpers use supplied `bindings.state` and `bindings.editable`, restrict proposals to configured `paths` and the current revision, and apply a replacement only after all configured `approvers` approve. An `acceptedNew` approval outcome can therefore mean an approval was recorded while the amendment remains pending.

Child preparation itself does not check acceptance or access readiness, initialize the child, or emit an activation event. A returned child is prepared configuration, not confirmation of consent, permission or active execution.
